incomplete_fix_quote: Zip Slip protections implemented in CVE-2023-24057 (GHSA-jqh6-9574-5x22) can be bypassed due to a partial path traversal vulnerability. In TerminologyCacheManager.java, `String path = Path.of(Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName())).normalize().toFile().getAbsolutePath();` -- while getAbsolutePath returns a normalized path, because the string path is not slash terminated, the guard `path.startsWith(targetDir)` can be bypassed to write the contents of the Zip file to a SIBLING directory of the cache directory. Consider "/usr/outnot".startsWith("/usr/out"): the check is bypassed although /outnot is not under the /out directory.
root_cause: org.hl7.fhir.r4b/r5 TerminologyCacheManager.unzip: the CVE-2023-24057 fix (5.6.92) normalizes the entry to an absolute path but still guards with String.startsWith(targetDir). A zip entry that Utilities.path resolves to a SIBLING directory whose name begins with the cache dir basename ('tx-cache') keeps the string prefix, so the guard passes and the file escapes the cache directory. 5.6.106 replaces the check with java.nio.file.Path#startsWith on normalized paths (component-wise), closing the sibling escape.

versions.v0_vulnerable: 5.6.90 (pre CVE-2023-24057 fix; guard = String path = Utilities.path(...); if(!path.startsWith(targetDir)))
versions.v1_incomplete: 5.6.92 (CVE-2023-24057 fix: normalize()+getAbsolutePath before same String.startsWith; the target)
